headline: TikTok is doing the work: $7.76 per install against $23 on Reddit. Instagram ended and isn't worth restarting as is.

nextAction.title: Move Reddit's remaining budget to a second TikTok cut
nextAction.why: Reddit has cost $23.33 per install over six installs; TikTok sits at $7.76 over 58. A second TikTok variant tests whether the friends angle or this specific edit is carrying the result.

tiktok-friends15s-v1.why: Cheapest install by a wide margin, and 29% of viewers make it past 2 seconds. Leave it running.

reddit-friends-square-v1.why: Clicks cost more than TikTok's ($0.57 vs $0.34) and only 2 in 100 clickers install. The static image isn't selling the room-code flow.

instagram-simplefun-reel-v1.why: Hook rate of 23% is below TikTok's 29%. The opening frame is a logo, not a hand of poker. Re-cut the first second before spending again.

tiktok-friends15s-v1.dropOff: Holds 40% from 2s to 6s, then thins out around the "Deal everyone in" beat.
notes: The question opener ("Poker night?") earns the 2-second hold.
The two "Deal everyone in" frames repeat; cutting one would land the win screen a second earlier.
The end card's "Come play." is small on a phone. Make it the biggest text on screen.

experiments.title: Win screen first
experiments.hypothesis: Opening on the "You win" moment hooks harder than the question, because the payoff is visible before anyone decides to scroll.
experiments.designPrompt: Make a 15-second vertical (1080x1920) ad for Downcard, a free poker app for playing with friends. No real money, no house. Open on the "You win" screen with chips sliding in, then rewind to show how the night started: "Start a table." "Share the code." "Deal everyone in." Use the existing warm yellow-to-teal gradient background and the real app screens. End card: "Simple, fun poker." with "Come play." as the largest text. Warm, simple, sincere tone. No casino imagery, no cash, no claims about winning money.
